AMDNR - NOTICE
==============

Copyright (c) 2026 3zwr1 (AMDNR)
Project:  https://github.com/3zwr1/AMD-NR---OptiScaler
Discord:  https://discord.gg/AMDNR

AMDNR runs DLSS 5 Neural Rendering on AMD Radeon GPUs, built into OptiScaler.
AMDNR is a fork of OptiScaler and is distributed under the GNU General Public
License version 3 (see LICENSE), together with the additional terms in sections
3 and 4 below. The AMDNR Launcher is the exception: see section 7.


1. What this notice covers
--------------------------

The following is AMDNR's own work, Copyright (c) 2026 3zwr1 (AMDNR):

  * every source file, shader and script written for AMDNR;
  * AMDNR's modifications to OptiScaler's files and to the other upstream code
    listed in section 5;
  * the release texts, menus and documentation written for AMDNR.

It covers every AMDNR release from 0.1.0 onward, including 0.3.3, 0.3.4, 0.3.5
and later, as recorded in CHANGELOG.md. Highlights:

  * AMDNR's AMD Neural Rendering pipeline: model interleave (Guided fill, Edit
    accumulation and the self-tuning interleave), the temporal stability pass,
    the residual controls (strength, limit, edge fade) with the Catmull-Rom
    resample and its ringing bound on the upstream residual resolve, NR
    resolution above 100% and dynamic NR resolution (the 25-100% NR resolution
    is upstream), the detail/colour and sharpen passes, the highlight proxy and
    its decode by the original, NR style presets, the HOME toggle default with
    its notice and input fix (the ToggleKey binding is upstream), the NR capture
    tool and the Neural tab.
  * The lmxxf runtime inside OptiScaler (0.3.0 and later): AMDNR's integration of
    lmxxf's network into OptiScaler's AMD path, the LmxxfNrRuntime.pak format,
    network history and passes, the edit shaper, auto-exposure, self-healing,
    the Vulkan-bridge warm-up, and the UE5 queue and command-list robustness.
  * The lmxxf RDNA 3 (RX 7000) backend (0.3.3) and its handheld builds for
    gfx1103 and gfx1150 (0.3.4); see AMDNR_RDNA3_BACKEND.txt.
  * The "c32w" one-wave C32 kernels for the lmxxf network on RDNA 4 (0.3.3.2;
    amdnr_c32w_family.hsaco in LmxxfNrRuntime.pak, SHA-256 pinned in
    LmxxfNrRuntime.dll), Copyright (c) 2026 3zwr1 (AMDNR). They run lmxxf's
    network (Kien, MIT; see lmxxf_LICENSE.txt). Acknowledgement: AMD's public
    RDNA 4 WMMA documentation (AMD GPUOpen, the ROCm matrix instruction
    calculator), used for ideas only; no code was taken from it.
  * AMDNR Anywhere (0.3.5): the capture-host mode of OptiScaler.dll - host
    detection, the Anywhere tab and its host settings, the host input path, the
    carry rules for a captured window, and the placement of the neural pass
    after upscaling ([DlssNr] AmdPlacement). The capture host itself is not
    part of this work (see section 5).
  * The Ray Regeneration tab, its backend and noise rules, the frame-generation
    tab rules (FgRestartNotice, FgPairRules, FgSwapchainReuse), the resize
    rules, the adapter and HIP-device rules, the shared runtime folder, the
    anti-cheat process rule, the mod-loader and ReShade detection (0.3.5).
  * The Anywhere host's output, edit, exposure and pacing rules, the style slot
    rules, the handheld highlight ceiling and pass rule, the game frame-
    generation provider rule, the HIP start-up evidence and the FSR 4 (INT8)
    handheld opt-in rules (0.3.5); and the loading of lmxxf 0.37's modules as a
    pinned group with its per-GPU defaults, off switches and fallbacks (the
    kernels and their launch code are lmxxf's, see section 5).
  * The 0.3.5 RDNA 3 module set of LmxxfNrRuntime.pak (the g2 operand-assembly
    build of lmxxf's kernels for gfx1100 / gfx1101 / gfx1102 / gfx1103): lmxxf's
    kernels (Kien, MIT), built by AMDNR with its own recipe; AMDNR claims the
    build, not the kernels.
  * The lmxxf network size tier policy (the tier snap and its RDNA 3 default),
    the small 360p / 576p network sizes, the per-GPU gating of handheld APUs,
    and the native character mask controls for lmxxf (0.3.4).
  * AMDNR's ports to lmxxf (0.3.4): Network output, Encoding, Residual edge
    fade, the Screen-space GI host, interleave pacing and the Game exposure
    switch; and for danielblnc's runtime: the runtime settings (Network style,
    Tone curve, Black lift, Game exposure), the highlight colour guard and the
    edit shaper modes.
  * The AMDNR menu of 0.3.4 (the rebuilt Neural tab and the shared look of every
    tab), Save report, the crash log, and the menu input fixes.
  * The integration of RenoDX's colour composition into both AMD runtimes (0.3.3;
    the maths is RenoDX's and the dlssnr.hlsl lineage's - Dagherbou, wilsjo2 - see
    RenoDX_ATTRIBUTION.txt and the CREDITS in amd/NrCompose.h).
  * The FSR Ray Regeneration path-traced profile, the SSS-guided skin smoothing
    and the Ray Regeneration A/B, tuning and diagnostic tools (0.3.3 - 0.3.4).
  * The graphics-state hooks and restore (GraphicsSnapshotHooks.h) on the
    upstream snapshot bookkeeping (GraphicsSnapshot.h); not installed in 0.3.3.
  * AMDNR Screen GI (0.3.4, preview; dlssnr/gi): screen-space ambient
    occlusion and one bounce of light, its shaders, host, menu rows and test
    harness. Written clean-room from published papers only; no code from the
    inherited Screen-space GI or any other project. Ideas from: Therrien,
    Levesque and Gilet 2023 (visibility bitmask screen-space indirect
    lighting); Jimenez, Wu, Pesce and Jarabo 2016 (GTAO and its multi-bounce
    fit); Jimenez 2014 (interleaved gradient noise); Roberts (the R2
    sequence); Schied et al. 2017 (SVGF); Dammertz et al. 2010 (edge-avoiding
    a-trous); Kopf et al. 2007 (joint bilateral upsampling); Karis 2014 and
    Salvi 2016 (history clamping); Turanszki 2019 and Wu 2020 (normals from
    depth); Hartley 1997 (rotating-camera self-calibration); IEC 61966-2-1
    (the sRGB transfer function).
  * The AMDNR Launcher: AMDNR's own work, under its own licence, not GPL-3.0
    (see section 7).


2. Where the credit lives
-------------------------

  * This file and AMDNR_RDNA3_BACKEND.txt in the Licenses folder.
  * The copyright lines at the top of AMDNR's source files, and the
    "Modifications Copyright (c) 2026 3zwr1 (AMDNR)" lines in the upstream files
    that AMDNR changed.
  * The version resource of OptiScaler.dll and LmxxfNrRuntime.dll
    (Properties > Details).
  * The credit notice at the start of LmxxfNrRuntime.pak, which the runtime
    authenticates.
  * The menu: the header's copyright line and the credits row under it.


3. Additional term (GNU GPL v3, section 7(b))
---------------------------------------------

For the material that AMDNR added to this work, the following additional term
applies, as permitted by section 7(b) of the GNU General Public License v3:

  Any copy, fork, port or derivative work that contains AMDNR material, in source
  or binary form, must preserve this notice and the copyright lines in AMDNR's
  source files, and must credit

      AMDNR by 3zwr1 - https://github.com/3zwr1/AMD-NR---OptiScaler

  in its README (or equivalent documentation) and wherever it shows credits or an
  About section.


4. The AMDNR menu (GNU GPL v3, section 7(b), (c) and (e))
---------------------------------------------------------

The AMDNR menu — its layout, design, texts and the code AMDNR added for it — is
Copyright (c) 2026 3zwr1 (AMDNR). It is part of this GPL-3.0 fork, with these
additional terms (GPL-3.0 section 7):

  (b) anyone who reuses any part of it must keep this copyright line and credit
      AMDNR by 3zwr1 visibly, in the menu and the README;
  (c) you may not present it, or a modified copy, as your own work; modified
      versions must be clearly marked as changed;
  (e) no rights are granted to the AMDNR name or logo; other projects may not
      use them.


5. What this notice does NOT cover
----------------------------------

AMDNR claims no copyright over the work of others. They keep their rights and
licences:

  * OptiScaler - the OptiScaler contributors (GPL-3.0).
  * Dagherbou (OptiScaler_DLSSNR), wilsjo2 (OptiScaler-DLSSNR-PreSR-Multipass),
    Matheus and TheAutomatic (dlss-5-amd-project) - the DLSS-NR and pre-SR code
    that AMDNR's base derives from, including the 25-100% NR resolution and its
    residual resolve, the graphics-state snapshot bookkeeping and the ToggleKey
    binding (GPL-3.0).
  * TheAutomatic - LmxxfNrRuntime.cpp, LmxxfNrApi.h, LmxxfProductionOptions.h:
    portions contributed to lmxxf by TheAutomatic (MIT). The lmxxf runtime
    integration of 0.3.0 builds on TheAutomatic's DLSS 5 AMD project work.
  * danielblnc - DLSS-NR on AMD by Daniel Blanco,
    https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD - the closed runtime. It ships in
    Runtime.zip, unmodified, with his permission and under its author's own
    terms (see danielblnc_ATTRIBUTION.txt).
  * lmxxf (Kien) - the lmxxf network port, kernels and runtime (MIT; see
    lmxxf_LICENSE.txt), https://github.com/lmxxf/dlss5-on-amd-9070xt-porting.
  * lmxxf (Kien) - the lmxxf 0.31 kernels in LmxxfNrRuntime.pak
    (the ViT projection (lmxxf031-vit-wide-deep), the C512 QKV and mix kernels (lmxxf031-c512-m32-mh, lmxxf031-c512-m32-deep) and one-wave-per-head attention (lmxxf031-c64-wave2)) are lmxxf's (MIT; lmxxf 0.31), built by AMDNR from lmxxf's
    sources and build recipe. AMDNR's part: loading, SHA-256 pins, per-GPU
    gating and fallbacks in LmxxfNrRuntime.dll.
  * lmxxf 0.37 by Kien (MIT) - the lmxxf 0.37 kernels in LmxxfNrRuntime.pak
    (the lmxxf037-* modules for gfx1200 / gfx1201, shipped as lmxxf built them)
    and the host launch code for them in LmxxfNrRuntime.dll are lmxxf's (MIT;
    see lmxxf_LICENSE.txt). AMDNR's part: loading them as one pinned group,
    SHA-256 pins, per-GPU defaults, off switches and fallbacks.
  * RenoDX by clshortfuse (Carlos Lopez Jr.) - the colour composition maths (MIT;
    see RenoDX_ATTRIBUTION.txt).
  * Zach Hembree (DarkHelmet) - FSR Ray Regeneration for OptiScaler (branch
    ffx-denoise-experimental), the origin of AMDNR's Ray Regeneration path;
    burak113 - the continuation of that branch AMDNR ported from (commit 3da4808,
    2026-09-19). Both GPL-3.0.
  * Coldwood1026 - XeFGUnlock, the base of the built-in XeFG multi-frame unlock
    (GPL-3.0).
  * Nukem9 - dlssg-to-fsr3 (GPL-3.0; see dlssg-to-fsr3_ATTRIBUTION.txt).
  * Screen-space GI (the inherited effect; retired from the Neural tab's menu in
    0.3.4, still available from the ini) - an effect AMDNR
    inherited from the OptiScaler-AMD-PreSR lineage; the credit belongs to its
    original authors. Its shaders come from the experimental_lighting folder of
    the danielblnc package, which AMDNR does not ship.
  * Magpie by Blinue, experimental fork by SAOG0721 (GPL-3.0), fetched from the
    author, not redistributed by AMDNR - the window-capture host AMDNR Anywhere
    runs inside. No Magpie source or binary is included with AMDNR; the AMDNR
    Launcher downloads the fork's release from its author. AMDNR's DLL only
    recognises the host by its process name and reads the settings the
    launcher wrote for it.
  * ReShade by crosire (BSD-3-Clause) - AMDNR detects ReShade beside it through
    ReShade's public add-on exports and its published unwrap interface GUID;
    no ReShade code is included.
  * AMD FidelityFX, Intel XeSS and Microsoft DirectX - under their own licences in
    this folder.
  * NVIDIA - DLSS and the neural network's design and weights belong to NVIDIA.
    AMDNR is not affiliated with NVIDIA or AMD.


6. Source code
--------------

AMDNR's source code will be published on GitHub with AMDNR 0.5.0.


7. The AMDNR Launcher
---------------------

The AMDNR Launcher's source is in Launcher/OpenSource/ of AMDNR's GitHub
repository. It is NOT covered by the repository's GPL-3.0 LICENSE or by the
additional terms above: it is source-available, all rights reserved,
Copyright (c) 2026 3zwr1 (AMDNR). See Launcher/OpenSource/LICENSE.txt. The
launcher's manifest is Launcher/manifest.json.
